opening_question_spark: If bones were metal, would your body become stronger?
book_transition: The answer appears as we explore a metal skeleton.
body: Metal bones could hold heavy loads with ease.
But a human skeleton needs flexible joints.
Real bones are strong and slightly bendable.
A metal frame would resist bending more than bone.
The body might become too heavy to move.
Muscles would struggle with a much heavier skeleton.
Metal bones could make repairs harder after damage.
Some implants use metals like titanium for support.
Strength alone cannot replace a living skeleton's balance.
full_narration: If bones were metal, would your body become stronger? The answer appears as we explore a metal skeleton. Metal bones could hold heavy loads with ease. But a human skeleton needs flexible joints. Real bones are strong and slightly bendable. A metal frame would resist bending more than bone. The body might become too heavy to move. Muscles would struggle with a much heavier skeleton. Metal bones could make repairs harder after damage. Some implants use metals like titanium for support.
